title: bug: a worktree completion whose push origin applied but answered [remote rejected] is routed unlanded and its receipt journal deleted, so the retry finds nothing to commit, no completion row is ever recorded, and QA's landed gate parks the row BLOCKED (both launchers)
description:
Filed by the governor at 22:50Z on 2026-11-03 after a live incident on task-7cef0861.

INCIDENT (all times Z, 2026-11-03):
- 22:41:06: worker-c9368191 takes the git-land lease for 7cef0861's completion.
- 22:41:38: the completion C = 890b1831 is created, and its push reaches origin. origin/moe/work-2026-10-24 holds 890b1831 to this hour. Its tree equals attempt-de9d1520's candidate tree bcc76403, its parent is the candidate base 3441d183, and its trailers are Moe-Task task-7cef0861 / Moe-Kind completion.
- 22:41:46-49: the wrapper still reads a `![remote rejected]` porcelain line. It records MOE_PUSH_FAILED and the rescue ref refs/moe/rescue/task-7cef0861.../20261103T224148Z (reason=remote), then finalizes the attempt unlanded. The row goes REVIEW -> WORKING with landingRetry remote.
- 22:43:55: the retry session (worker-33f67e5b) finds the merged tree equal to the target's: MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, with no completion row.
- 22:44:34: QA's landed gate (qa_landed_gate) stops: "no recorded completion commit (get_context task.landing.lastCompletion.sha is missing ...)". The row is BLOCKED.
- 22:46:42: the governor repairs it by hand with record_commit (890b1831, verified against the candidate).
Without that manual repair the row cannot leave the loop: every new landing finds nothing to commit, and QA blocks again.

CAUSE (at tip 15728974):
- scripts/moe-agent.sh wt_push_target (:7488-7498) maps a `![remote rejected]` line straight to rc 2. wt_publish (:7504-7520) then runs `rm -f` on the receipt journal and sets MOE_PUSH_FAILED. Neither ever fetches to check whether origin took C, which reconcile_push (:7418) does for every unknown answer.
- The retry's L5 branch (:7581-7584) already recovers a journaled C when the merged tree equals the target's ($jc gives LAND_WT_RECOVERED and records the owed completion row). The journal is gone by then, so it records a plain "nothing".
- The ps1 twins behave the same: Send-MoeLandPush (:7094-7105), Publish-MoeWorktreeLanding (:7112 on), and the L5 branch (:7220-7223).
GitHub can answer a push with remote rejected (an internal error or a ref-lock timeout on its side) after applying the update. So a single remote-rejected line is not proof that C is absent.

FIX DIRECTION (the planner decides):
1. On `![remote rejected]`, fetch origin's target once, the same way reconcile_push does. If C is an ancestor of origin's tip, treat the push as published (rc 0: journal 'pushed', mirror, record and finalize landed). Otherwise MOE_PUSH_FAILED as today. A failed fetch stays MOE_PUSH_FAILED.
2. Optionally, as defense in depth, keep the receipt journal until that check proves C absent, so a pre-flight replay or the retry's L5 recovery can still owe the row.
Both launchers, in string parity. Sync the worktree landing text in scripts/CLAUDE.md (it says "`[remote rejected]` is `MOE_PUSH_FAILED`") and the design doc's L9 line if it says the same.

PLACEMENT: edit only the push/publish functions named above. The CQ-M07n rows (23c803d2 WORKING, 62ec51f1 gated) and cc4213c0 edit the VM-route blocks of the same files, and merge-tree lands separate hunks cleanly. In the task worktree, edit moe-agent.{sh,ps1} in place with a TOOL-witnessed editor, then bash -n and the ps1 ParseFile check, never temp+mv. Test with a git stub or fake remote in the worktree landing harness (scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs): the push updates the bare remote, then prints a `![remote rejected]` porcelain line.
definitionOfDone: In both launchers, a worktree completion whose push answers `![remote rejected]` while origin's target already contains C is treated as published: the attempt is finalized landed with landedRevision C, a completion row with pushed:true is recorded, no rescue ref or landingRetry is created, and the receipt journal is settled rather than deleted unread.

A `![remote rejected]` answer where origin's target does NOT contain C after the re-check (and a failed re-check fetch) still ends MOE_PUSH_FAILED with the rescue ref and the unlanded remote route exactly as before; parity-check passes and the landing harness covers both cases on the sh and ps1 wrappers.
scripts/CLAUDE.md's worktree landing text (and the design doc's L9 line, if it states the old rule) describes the re-check.

implementationPlan.description:
Fix (DoD 1, 2). Edit only the push functions. The VM-route blocks belong to other open rows: CQ-M07n/n3 in ps1, task-1ccae85c/cc4213c0 in sh.

scripts/moe-agent.sh
- Add a helper above wt_push_target (~:7488): `wt_remote_holds TARGET C`.
  - It runs land_fetch "$1" (3 tries, the backoff apart), then `git -C "$MOE_TOP" merge-base --is-ancestor "$2" "refs/remotes/origin/$1^{commit}"`.
  - It returns 0 only on that proof; a failed fetch or any other exit is 1.
  - It never pushes.
- In wt_push_target, after the porcelain loop, add `if [ "$rc" = 2 ] && wt_remote_holds "$1" "$3"; then`. That branch prints `[WARN] MOE_PUSH_REMOTE_REJECTED_APPLIED: origin answered [remote rejected] for $3, but origin's $1 holds it; the push counts as published.` and sets rc=0. The line carries no task id, because migration landing shares this function.
- Fix the header comments of wt_push_target and wt_publish, which call 2 just "[remote rejected]".
- Leave wt_publish unchanged. rc 0 takes the normal path: journal 'pushed …', mirror, LAND_PUSHED, then the row and the landed finalize. rc 2 still removes the journal and sets MOE_PUSH_FAILED, now only after the re-check found no C or its fetch failed.
- Migration's `2)` arm is unchanged. It inherits the re-check, so a push that was applied there ends MOE_MIGRATION_LANDED.

scripts/moe-agent.ps1 (twins)
- Add `Test-MoeRemoteHolds([string]$Top, [string]$T, [string]$C)`: Invoke-MoeLandFetch, then rev-parse and `merge-base --is-ancestor` through Invoke-MoeGit. It returns $true only on proof.
- In Send-MoeLandPush's `![remote rejected]` branch (~:7101), keep setting $script:MoePushDetail, then `if (Test-MoeRemoteHolds $Top $T $C) { Write-Host '<the same line, byte-identical>' -ForegroundColor Yellow; return 0 }; return 2`.
- Fix the header comments. Publish-MoeWorktreeLanding and the migration caller are unchanged.

Error handling: a failed or unprovable re-check keeps today's MOE_PUSH_FAILED route exactly. No re-push, no new round, no force flag.

The new MOE_PUSH_ code sits in both wrappers, so parity's family compare passes; parity-check.{sh,ps1}, held by another row, need no edit. Keep moe-agent.ps1's UTF-8 BOM.

Edit your worktree copies in place with a TOOL-witnessed editor; never temp+mv. Then run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` and the ps1 ParseFile check: powershell.exe -NoProfile with Parser::ParseFile on the wslpath -w path, exit 1 on any error.

Docs (DoD 3).

scripts/CLAUDE.md, the L9-L10 bullet of **Land on every exit, worktree mode** (~:25): replace "`[remote rejected]` is `MOE_PUSH_FAILED`" with the re-check rule. A `[remote rejected]` answer gets one re-check fetch:
- An origin target that holds C counts as published (`MOE_PUSH_REMOTE_REJECTED_APPLIED`, then the usual row and `landed` finalize), because a remote can refuse after applying the update.
- Otherwise, or when that fetch fails, it is `MOE_PUSH_FAILED`, unlanded `remote`, as before.

docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md: state the same rule in the L9 row (~:121), the 2.5 unlanded-route list (~:132: "a `[remote rejected]` push that the re-check fetch does not show applied") and the L9 summary (~:179).

Touch no other doc text. docs/CONFIGURATION.md's MOE_PUSH_FAILED row (~:271) stays true as written and is outside this row's 5-file budget; leave it.

Verify once (DoD 2), from the task worktree root, after the last edit:
`cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && E=$(env | awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ", $1}') && T=scripts/tests A=scripts/moe-agent N="/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" P="env $E powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File" && export MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=wt-remote-rejected,wt-unlanded,wt-push,wt-completion,wt-replay-remote,codes WSLENV=MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY && S=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/bc6b-v.XXXXXX) && cp $T/postflight-fake-proxy.js $S/fp.js && w(){ wslpath -w "$1"; } && x(){ env $E node $T/$1 sh "$PWD/$A.sh" $S/fp.js $S "$BASH" && env $E "$N" "$(w $T/$1)" ps1 "$(w $A.ps1)" "$(w $S/fp.js)" "$(w $S)" powershell; } && bash -n $A.sh && bash $T/parity-check.sh && $P "$(w $T/parity-check.ps1)" && x postflight-worktree.cjs && x postflight-migration.cjs && env $E bash $T/worktree-landing.sh && $P "$(w $T/worktree-landing.ps1)"`

Its fresh output is the complete_task evidence.
- The command is task-d2d6ac4b's DONE gate pattern.
- The scratch dir sits on /mnt/d: a /tmp cwd breaks the Windows legs (mem:gotcha-qa-ps1-postflight-from-wsl).
- The migration suite runs too, because migration shares the push function.
- If the run passes the 600 s foreground cap, launch it in the background into a log and poll for the end, per mem:gotcha-qa-session-env-and-signals-leak-into-harness.
- Don't edit the wrappers mid-run (mem:gotcha-editing-wrapper-while-harness-runs).
- Kill only PIDs your session recorded.

Error handling for a red run:
- If a Windows leg fails, rerun it on HEAD's scripts before blaming the change.
- Fix the cause in step 1's or step 2's file, never by weakening a case or touching worktree-landing.{sh,ps1}.
- Then re-run the whole command.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
In both launchers, a worktree landing push answered `![remote rejected]` gets ONE re-check: a fetch of origin's target, then an ancestry test. This covers the completion push and the human-run migration landing, which shares the function.
- When origin's target holds C, the push counts as published: a MOE_PUSH_REMOTE_REJECTED_APPLIED warning, the journal marked 'pushed …', the mirror, a pushed:true completion row and a landed finalize. No rescue ref, no landingRetry.
- When it does not, or the fetch fails, MOE_PUSH_FAILED and the unlanded remote route run exactly as before.
acceptanceCriteria: On both the sh and ps1 wrappers, the wt-remote-rejected applied arm lands C: finalize landed, a pushed:true row, no rescue ref, no landingRetry, and the journal settled.
On both wrappers, the fetch-fails arm and wtUnlanded's pre-receive 'rejected' arm still route MOE_PUSH_FAILED, unlanded remote.
worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} and postflight-migration.cjs pass unchanged; parity-check.{sh,ps1} pass.
invariants: After [remote rejected]: never a re-push, a new round or a force flag.
Only proof (ancestry on a fetched origin tip) turns rc 2 into published.
The `[rejected]`, unknown and reconcile_push paths are unchanged.
The ps1 UTF-8 BOM is kept, and the new line's text is identical in both wrappers.
compatibility: Migration landing gains the same re-check through the shared push function.
No change to parity-check.{sh,ps1} or worktree-landing.{sh,ps1}.
approvedScope: sh: wt_remote_holds (new), wt_push_target, and the comments of wt_push_target and wt_publish
ps1: Test-MoeRemoteHolds (new), Send-MoeLandPush and its comments
Harness: the WT_GIT_PUSH_REMOTE_REJECTED and WT_GIT_FETCH_FAIL_AFTER_PUSH stub knobs; case wt-remote-rejected
Docs: the scripts/CLAUDE.md L9-L10 bullet; the design doc's L9 row, 2.5 list and L9 summary
reuse: land_fetch / Invoke-MoeLandFetch, and the merge-base ancestry test reconcile_push already uses.
wtUnlanded's bare() helper and its 'rejected' assertions.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Re-check in wt_publish only. Rejected: the shared push function's rc 2 would still lie to the migration landing. Fixing wt_push_target/Send-MoeLandPush makes 'remote rejected' mean refused AND absent everywhere.
2. Route [remote rejected] into reconcile_push. Rejected: reconcile_push re-pushes while the tip is B, but the held-out remoteRejected case pins exactly one push, and the DoD keeps the refused path as before.
3. Keep the journal when the re-check fetch fails. Rejected: the DoD fixes that path as MOE_PUSH_FAILED, exactly as before. Residual, for QA to know, not to fix here: if that fetch fails while origin holds C, the incident loop can recur.
4. A server-side hook as the test fixture. Impossible: pre-receive can only refuse before the update. The PATH stub does the real push, then prints the line, which matches the description's suggestion.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- land_fetch already retries 3 times; the re-check adds no loop of its own.
- wt_publish's journal handling is correct once rc is truthful.
- The `codes` case compares only the WORKTREE/LAND/CONTROL/BOARD/MIGRATION/SERENA_IGNORE families. MOE_PUSH_* is compared by parity-check.sh.
- worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} are held-out WT-08T acceptance suites, run in CI. Their remoteRejected case asserts one push and the tracking ref still at B0. A single successful re-check fetch keeps both true.
planningNotes.risks:
- Files shared with other open rows: touch only the push functions, so merge-tree lands separate hunks.
- The ps1 stub runs in-process: porcelain goes on the success stream, failures through Write-Error.
- The Windows legs need a /mnt/d scratch dir and no MOE_*/CLAUDE* leakage (the `env $E` prefix, plus WSLENV for MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY).
- A long run past the tool cap needs background-plus-poll.
- A stub knob that also matches the L4 fetch would break both arms. That is why the push, not the case, creates the fetch-fail marker.
